   649	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
   650	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |

   673	## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout
   674	
   675	**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
   676	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
   677	attacks.
   678	
   679	**On Papaya's stack**
   680	
   681	- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); a platform team or named
   682	  engineers (deploy workflows, rulesets, pipelines; whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
   683	  Applicability); engineering leads (decide CODEOWNERS content; changes to it are approved by the L3 owner team); engineering management (on-call schedule).
   684	- **Policy as code:** catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are files under
   685	  CODEOWNERS. Settings that live outside files are kept as an expected copy in git and compared with
   686	  the live state: GitHub settings (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8) and Claude managed settings, which are edited in
   687	  the admin console (📖 R1.1.5; comparison method in layer 2). Few GitHub admins and Claude org
   688	  Owners, reviewed quarterly.
   689	- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
   690	  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (OD1; layer 2).
   691	- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed): [`03-rollout-plan.md`](03-rollout-plan.md), moved
   692	  there unchanged. Order (framing Q8): (1) remove long-lived CI credentials, (2) narrow standing prod
   693	  access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2). Phase 1 (0–30 days)
   694	  makes the PR the only prod write path, with six hard prerequisites before standing prod write is
   695	  removed; phase 2 (30–60) adds SCPs, the rest of the managed baseline and automated
   696	  reconciliation; phase 3 (60–90) tests and reviews. The phase-1 load on 1–2 DevSecOps people is the
   697	  main rollout risk [design; effort not estimated ⚠️].
   698	
   699	- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry.
   700	- **Standards mapping:** ISO 27001:2022 Annex A (IDs recalled, ⚠️ R5.1), HIPAA Security Rule
   701	  (📖 R5.2) and Vietnam law (📖 R5.4) are mapped per control area in the
   702	  [compliance register](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference), with every caveat. "A named human approves"
   703	  is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement (⚠️ R5.7 #1).
   704	- **Out of scope:** security of the production AI agents (A7a); noted as a follow-up.
   705	
   706	**Audit evidence.** Git history of policy files, monthly metrics, 90-day review minutes, the exception register and planted-injection reports; standards: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference).
   707	
   708	**Cost / value.** Steady, small overhead for DevSecOps and the owners of deploy workflows. Compliance gets a managed system
   709	with owners and review dates.

137	   136	## Limits of the risk stop
138	   137	
139	   138	The risk stop answers one framework problem: on GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before
140	   139	apply (framework §1). It catches **risky prod diffs that nobody looked at**. It is not a boundary
141	   140	against **malicious or prompt-injected code that was approved**:
142	   141	
143	   142	- The stack's own code runs with the prod deploy role: `npm` packages are installed before the
144	   143	  credentials (so install scripts get none), but the Pulumi program runs during `preview` and
145	   144	  `up`, and Serverless plugins during `package`/`diff`/`deploy`. That code could call AWS
146	   145	  directly, or tamper with files the classifier reads, in the same job. The defence against it
147	   146	  is the PR review itself, and from phase 2 IAM Access Analyzer and policy packs (layer 5).
148	   147	- A stronger variant [design, not in the framework]: preview with a separate prod **preview**
149	   148	  role (read and state access, no write), run the classifier in its own job on a fresh
150	   149	  checkout without credentials, and assume the deploy role only in a later job after the stop.
151	   150	  It adds a role and a job split; it is an open question for the owner.
152	   151	- `pulumi up` previews again before applying. A change made outside the pipeline between the
153	   152	  two previews (JIT, drift) is not re-checked. `pulumi preview --save-plan` + `pulumi up --plan`
154	   153	  would bind the two, but update plans are experimental (📖 R4.1.3).
155	   154	- Concurrency: a running deploy is never cancelled, but GitHub cancels a run that is still
156	   155	  pending when a newer one arrives for the same group (📖 GitHub docs source,
157	   156	  `data/reusables/actions/actions-group-concurrency.md`). Some merged commits therefore have no
158	   157	  deploy run of their own; the newer run deploys them too, and the change record must link both
159	   158	  commits to that run. `queue: max` would give every commit its own run, but the same page says
160	   159	  the order "is not guaranteed": an older commit could then deploy after a newer one and undo it
161	   160	  in prod. So the default is kept on purpose [design].
162	   161	- The type lists are examples. For types that are missing, the rule on property names
163	   162	  (`policy`, `role`, `securityGroup`, `vpcConfig`, `public`, `authorization`, `logging`, …;
164	   163	  a narrower set on creates) catches some changes, not all.
165	   164	- **Code in the deploy job can act as any prod deploy role.** `id-token: write` is job-wide, so
166	   165	  install scripts, the Pulumi program and Serverless plugins can request the job's OIDC token
167	   166	  (⚠️ from memory of GitHub's OIDC docs) and assume either deploy role, since both trust the same
168	   167	  subject. The two-role split and the install-before-credentials order stop drift and honest
169	   168	  mistakes, not malicious approved code. Phase-2 roadmap with OD15: a build job without
170	   169	  `id-token`, and per-role environments (different subjects) or `job_workflow_ref` (G10).
171	   170	- **Open gap:** nothing proves that a deploy really stopped at `stopped_commit` with the
172	   171	  approved hash. An approval merged early (naming a commit whose deploy did not stop, with a
173	   172	  hash computed in advance, which needs knowledge of prod inputs) is accepted if a later change
174	   173	  **outside** the stack's directory, such as a shared library, produces exactly that diff. Changes
175	   174	  inside the stack's directory are rejected. Watching the whole repository instead would cancel
176	   175	  every approval at each unrelated merge in a monorepo. The fix is for the approval-gate app to
177	   176	  check, on the approval PR, that the stopped run's summary carries the same hash (G19) [design].
178	   177	  `test_known_gap_early_approval_and_change_outside_the_stack` documents the current behaviour.
179	   178	- The approver of the approval PR sees **which** prod resources and properties change, not the
180	   179	  new values (the summary never prints values, to keep secrets out of logs). The values are
181	   180	  reviewed in the code of the stopped PR. Framework layer 3 and ADR-0004 say the approver "sees
182	   181	  the prod diff"; that wording is too strong and is corrected in the framework's final pass.
183	   182	- Any commit to the stack's directory between the stop and the approval merge cancels the
184	   183	  approval: the author names the newer stopped commit and the owner approves again. In an
185	   184	  incident that is one more review round.
186	   185	- `npm ci` runs before the credentials, but its lifecycle scripts can still write to
187	   186	  `$GITHUB_ENV` / `$GITHUB_PATH` and so influence later steps that hold them.
188	   187	  `npm ci --ignore-scripts` reduces this where the stack's packages allow it.
189	   188	- If the newest merge to `main` carries `[skip ci]` (or similar) in its message, no push run
190	   189	  exists for the tip and the older runs refuse to deploy; prod stays behind until the next merge
191	   190	  (📖 GitHub docs source, `content/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/skip-workflow-runs.md`,
192	   191	  via review). Operator action: merge an empty change.
193	   192	- Within 7 days, an approved change that is reverted and then merged again with identical code
194	   193	  passes without a new approval. This is intended: it is the same code and the same prod diff
195	   194	  that an owner approved.
196	   195	- The binding relies on squash-only merges (`ruleset-main.json`); with merge commits, a PR's
197	   196	  inner commits would be invisible to the first-parent check.

200	   199	
201	   200	Points the framework text does not yet say; carried into the framework in the final pass.
202	   201	Owner decisions 2026-11-09 (framework OD14–OD18): findings 1, 3 and 4 accepted; the risk stop keeps
203	   202	its current scope (OD15); the early-approval gap is an accepted limit for G19 to close (OD18).
204	   203	Step 2: finding 16 accepted (OD19); the job-wide OIDC token limit goes to the phase-2 roadmap
205	   204	with OD15 (OD20).
206	   205	
207	   206	1. **The risk-stop classifier must be an L3 path** [design]. The deploy runs it from the merged
208	   207	   commit, so a PR that edits it together with an IAM change, approved by the domain team, could
209	   208	   switch the stop off. `CODEOWNERS` adds `/tools/risk-stop/` to the L3 owner team. Needs owner
210	   209	   confirmation: it extends the canonical L3 list of framework layer 5.
211	   210	2. **An approval must be bound to git history, not only to a hash** [design]. Two review rounds
212	   211	   found ways for one PR to carry its own risky change and approval, or for an approval to be
213	   212	   reused. Rules now: read from git objects only; file named `<stopped_commit>.yaml`, never
214	   213	   edited; stopped commit and approval commit both on `main`'s first-parent history, in that
215	   214	   order; the approval commit touches only `deploy-approvals/<stack>/`; the stack's directory
216	   215	   and the classifier unchanged since the stopped commit; at most 7 days old.
217	   216	3. **Squash-only merges** [design]: `ruleset-main.json` allows only squash, so each PR is one
218	   217	   commit on `main`. Cost: PR-internal history is not kept on `main`.
219	   218	4. **Deploy only the tip of `main`** [design]: people with write access can re-run a workflow run
220	   219	   for up to 30 days, with the same `GITHUB_SHA` (📖 GitHub docs source,
221	   220	   `content/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs.md`, via review). An
222	   221	   old deploy run re-run would roll prod back without any approval. `deploy-prod.yml` stops unless
223	   222	   the run's commit is the current tip of `main`, read with `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/ref/heads/main`
224	   223	   (✅ branch-only form; `commits/main` could resolve to a tag named `main`). This is a new
225	   224	   condition for framework layer 3's "merge approval = deploy approval" list.
226	   225	5. **Classification beyond the framework's categories** [design]: the property-name rule, the
227	   226	   audit/detection category and "an unknown operation stops" go beyond layer 3's list
228	   227	   (stateful replace/delete, IAM, network, policy finding).
229	   228	6. **The approval hash must cover changed values**, not only resource names, or an approval for
230	   229	   one IAM policy would let a different change to the same policy through; and it must leave out
231	   230	   values that change on every build, or an approval never matches. ⚠️ From memory, not checked:
232	   231	   Serverless puts a timestamped path in the Lambda `Code.S3Key` and a code hash in
233	   232	   `AWS::Lambda::Version` logical IDs; both are left out of the hash.
234	   233	7. **Fail-safe CODEOWNERS default** [design]: without it, root `package.json`, a new stack or a new
235	   234	   `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` folder would be unowned, and GitHub then accepts an approval from
236	   235	   any writer (📖 about code owners).
237	   236	8. **Same-repository reusable workflows can use `uses: $/.github/workflows/<file>`**, which GitHub
238	   237	   now recommends: it resolves to the running commit, not to the runner's workspace (📖 GitHub docs
239	   238	   source, `data/reusables/actions/reusable-workflow-calling-syntax.md`; flagged by zizmor's
240	   239	   `self-repository` audit). `actionlint` 1.7.12 (✅ latest release on 2026-11-09, published
241	   240	   2026-03-30) does not know the syntax; `validate.sh` ignores only that message.
242	   241	9. **`runner.temp` is not available in job-level `env`** (✅ caught by `actionlint`); paths use
243	   242	   `$RUNNER_TEMP` inside steps.

311	   310	    therefore check keys by path and require a documentation source for every key it lacks.
312	   311	19. **The phase-1 allowlist gives no protection for `~/.aws`, and a "read-only" wildcard rule
313	   312	    can write files** (review step 3): Claude Code runs a built-in set of read-only commands
314	   313	    (`cat`, `grep`, `head`, read-only `git` …) without a prompt in every mode, and the set is not
315	   314	    configurable (📖 [permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md#read-only-commands)).
316	   315	    Leaving `cat` out of the allowlist protected nothing. Worse, `Bash(git log *)`, `Bash(git show *)`
317	   316	    and `Bash(git diff *)` also match `--output=<path>`, which writes chosen content to any path
318	   317	    (✅ git 2.34.1; the docs use `git log --output=<file>` as an example match). The allowlist is now
319	   318	    two exact repo scripts, and those run whatever `package.json` says [limit]. Owner decision OD21
320	   319	    adds two keys to phase 1: a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule, which also applies to recognized
321	   320	    `cat`/`head`/`tail` (📖 permissions), and `autoMode.classifyAllShell` (📖, ≥ 2.1.193), so the two
322	   321	    allow rules do not skip the auto-mode classifier. Left open until the phase-2 sandbox: a command
323	   322	    that reads files without naming them (`grep -r` from `~`) or a script that opens `~/.aws` itself
324	   323	    is not covered by a deny rule (📖 permissions). Not chosen: `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`

    84	## Evidence for one prod change (S8)
    85	
    86	**Target** (framing §5): for a prod change picked at random, show who proposed, who approved, what
    87	was approved, what was applied and when, in ≤ 30 minutes, without asking anyone. Not yet timed
    88	(⚠️; first measured in rollout).
    89	
    90	Start **backward**, from a prod write in CloudTrail: unlike starting from a PR, this also finds
    91	unapproved writes, as the monthly reconciliation does (S3).
    92	
    93	| Step | Question | Record | Where |
    94	|---|---|---|---|
    95	| 1 | What was applied, when? | Write event: `eventTime`, `eventName`, resource; session name `deploy-<run_id>-<attempt>` [design, E3] in `principalId` (📖 R2.5.3) | CloudTrail; digests prove integrity (📖 R2.6.4) |
    96	| 2 | Which run? | Run ID → deploy run: stack, commit SHA, preview, risk-stop result | Actions log (⚠️ G7; export Ph 2) |
    97	| 3 | What was approved? | SHA → squash-merged PR (OD16). Stale approvals are dismissed (📖 R3.2.3), so approval covers the final diff | GitHub PR |
    98	| 4 | Who proposed? | PR author; for an app-opened PR, the person who triggered it, from the approval-gate check (G19) | GitHub PR |
    99	| 5 | Who approved, before apply? | Review name and time; approver ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (📖 R3.2.3, R3.3.1); approver owns the path (CODEOWNERS at that commit). Approval < merge < `eventTime` | GitHub PR; git |
   100	| 6 | Was the gate on? | E1 copy; no `repository_ruleset.update` or `protected_branch.policy_override` in the window; G8 results | git; audit-log export |
   101	| 7 | Did the risk stop fire? | `risk-summary`; `deploy-approvals/` PR with hash and stack-owner approval; second run shows the hash matched | artifact (⚠️ G7); git; PR |

   103	From Ph 2 the change record (C-19) holds these links, so steps 2–7 are one lookup. In Ph 1 there is
   104	no change record, export or reconciliation: the auditor follows links by hand, and old records may be
   105	gone (audit log 180 days, 📖 R3.5.6; Actions ⚠️ G7). S8 is realistic only from Ph 2 (⚠️ inference).
   106	
   107	**Serverless stacks:** CloudFormation makes the changes with the stack's `deploymentRole` (layer 3),
   108	so those events may not carry the run's session name (⚠️ not researched). The link is the deploy
   109	session's CloudFormation call plus the stack's events.
   110	
   111	**Incident lane:** the same chain, plus the `incident` label and the on-call schedule showing the
   112	approver was the primary on shift, or the backup while the primary was unavailable (O-7). The wait
   113	(S7) runs from review request to approval. In Ph 1 the approver is called by phone, so paging time is
   114	not recorded (G5).
   115	
   116	**JIT fallback**, keyed by the JIT request ID ([layer 7](01-framework.md#layer-7--observability-audit-incident-response-and-break-glass)):
   117	(1) proposed: command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel independent of GitHub (O-1);
   118	(2) approved: on-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant; (3) granted: `CreateAccountAssignment`
   119	and `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2); (4) applied: CloudTrail writes of the
   120	`InfraOperator-<service>` session, the human named by session name and directory lookup, not a
   121	stable key (⚠️ R2.5.3); (5) reconciled: writes compared with the list, codify PR merged, drift
   122	ticket until then. The approver approved a **command list**, not the applied change; a write outside
   123	the list is found afterwards, not prevented.

## 4. Giả định

Đề không nói những điều dưới đây. Mỗi mục là **[GĐ]**: tôi dùng nó để thiết kế, chưa được xác nhận.
Mục nào "chịu lực" (đổi giả định thì đổi thiết kế) được đánh dấu ★.

| ID | Giả định | Vì sao cần | Nếu sai thì |
|---|---|---|---|
| GĐ-1 ★ ✔ | Đội engineering khoảng 20–60 người. Chưa có đội security riêng; DevSecOps là 1–2 người. Thiết kế không được để một người làm reviewer duy nhất. | Quyết định ai có thể là reviewer và kiểm soát nặng đến đâu thì gánh nổi. | Đội nhỏ hơn: cần cơ chế duyệt không phụ thuộc vào một người. Đội lớn hơn: có thể phân tầng reviewer. |
| GĐ-2 ★ ✔ | AWS có ít nhất một ranh giới account giữa prod và non-prod (AWS Organizations). Đăng nhập qua IAM Identity Center ("SSO profiles" trong đề). | Phân quyền theo môi trường cần ranh giới. | Nếu prod và non-prod chung account: tách account trở thành điều kiện tiên quyết, kéo dài lộ trình. |
| GĐ-3 | Dữ liệu các tenant cách ly logic (schema/bucket/prefix) trong cùng account, không phải account riêng cho từng tenant. | Ảnh hưởng tới khả năng giới hạn quyền theo tenant. | Nếu mỗi tenant một account: phân quyền theo tenant dễ hơn nhiều. |
| GĐ-4 | k0s chạy trên hạ tầng AWS (EC2); engineer truy cập bằng kubeconfig, chưa có SSO cho cluster. | Xác định k0s là đường thay đổi riêng cần kiểm soát. | Nếu đã có OIDC cho cluster: phần k0s nhẹ hơn. |
| GĐ-5 ★ ✔ (đã đổi 2026-11-08) | **Giả định của owner, không phải sự thật về Papaya:** Papaya dùng gói GitHub **Team**, không phải Enterprise. Theo docs (`work/02-research.md` 3.1.2, ✅), trên Team thì required reviewers của environment chỉ có cho repo public. Vì vậy monorepo private **không** có cổng duyệt ở environment. | Xác định chỗ đặt cổng duyệt: merge PR vào `main`, ép bằng rulesets (có trên Team cho repo private; 02-research 3.2.1, 3.6 #1, 3.7 A1). Environment `production` chỉ giới hạn branch = `main`. | Nếu Papaya dùng Enterprise Cloud: thêm required reviewers, prevent self-review và chặn admin bypass cho environment `production`. Chỉ đổi cấu hình, không đổi workflow (suy luận, 02-research 3.7 A1). |
| GĐ-6 ★ ✔ | **Coi laptop là không tin cậy.** Kiểm soát chính đặt ở cloud/CI. Cấu hình Claude Code do tổ chức đẩy xuống (managed settings, plugin marketplace) chỉ là lớp thứ hai. ⚠️ Gói Team Premium hỗ trợ ép cấu hình đến đâu chưa kiểm tra; sẽ kiểm ở bước thiết kế và đánh dấu 📖. | Quyết định chính sách cho agent là "ép" hay chỉ "khuyến nghị". | Nếu ép được tốt: lớp thứ hai mạnh hơn, nhưng thiết kế vẫn không dựa vào nó. |
| GĐ-7 | Laptop được quản lý tập trung (MDM) ở mức tối thiểu. | Một số kiểm soát cấu hình cần kênh đẩy xuống máy. | Không có MDM: càng phải dựa vào GĐ-6 hoặc kiểm soát phía server. |
| GĐ-8 ★ ✔ (đã đổi) | **Mọi thay đổi prod phải được duyệt trước khi áp dụng, kể cả trong sự cố.** Không có ngoại lệ "làm trước, duyệt sau" (break-glass không duyệt). Người dùng đã bác đề xuất ban đầu (cho phép một tập thao tác khẩn cấp, review sau). | Đây là ràng buộc cứng của Compliance. Hệ quả: trong sự cố, việc duyệt phải **nhanh và luôn có người duyệt**, 24/7. | — (đã là quyết định). Hệ quả cần thiết kế: người duyệt trực ngoài giờ, đường duyệt rút gọn cho thao tác khẩn cấp. Xem mâu thuẫn với ưu tiên 30 ngày ở mục 6. |
| GĐ-9 ★ ✔ (đã chỉnh) | **Mặc định agent không đọc dữ liệu thật** (MED/NID/BANK) trên prod, chỉ đọc metadata: config, metrics, log đã che dữ liệu. **Ngoại lệ theo từng trường hợp**, khi có thoả thuận phù hợp (BAA/DPA, hợp đồng với partner) và có người duyệt, vì có lúc debug bắt buộc phải xem dữ liệu thật. | Quyết định agent có được đọc dữ liệu prod hay không. | — (đã là quyết định). Hệ quả cần thiết kế: một đường xin quyền đọc dữ liệu có thời hạn, có phạm vi tenant, có duyệt và có log. |
| GĐ-10 | Pulumi dùng một backend có preview (`pulumi preview`) chạy được trong CI. Serverless deploy hiện chạy cả từ CI lẫn từ laptop. | Reviewer cần thấy trước thay đổi. | Nếu chỉ chạy từ laptop: phải chuyển deploy về CI trước. |
| GĐ-11 ★ ✔ | **Reviewer không phải là người làm.** "Người làm" gồm tác giả của thay đổi và agent đã tạo ra thay đổi (four-eyes). Một agent độc lập (không phải agent tạo thay đổi) **được** làm bước review tự động bổ sung, nhưng **không** được tính là phê duyệt. Phê duyệt chính thức ("named person" của Compliance) luôn là người. | Định nghĩa vai trò reviewer. | — (đã là quyết định). |
| GĐ-12 | Lộ trình triển khai framework khoảng 90 ngày, làm song song với chuẩn bị ISO 27001. Không có ngân sách lớn cho công cụ mới; ưu tiên tính năng sẵn có của stack hiện tại. | Định cỡ đề xuất và thứ tự ưu tiên. | Có ngân sách: có thể thêm công cụ chuyên dụng (vẫn không thay IaC/CI theo đề). |
| GĐ-13 | Yêu cầu theo quốc gia (VN, TH, HK) có thể khác nhau về nơi lưu trữ và xử lý dữ liệu; chưa biết chi tiết. | Framework cần chỗ cho chính sách theo tenant/quốc gia. | Chi tiết pháp lý phải do Compliance/Legal xác nhận; tôi không suy diễn luật cụ thể. |
| GĐ-14 ★ ✔ | **Non-prod (dev/staging) chỉ chứa dữ liệu synthetic hoặc đã che**, không có dữ liệu thật của khách hàng. Framework thêm một yêu cầu: không copy dữ liệu prod xuống non-prod. | Đây là điều kiện để vòng lặp non-prod của agent được tự do, không cần duyệt (S4c). | — (đã là quyết định). Nếu thực tế staging đang có bản copy prod, phải dọn trước. Trong lúc chưa dọn, non-prod theo quy tắc đọc dữ liệu của GĐ-9. |

---

## 5. Tiêu chí thành công

Đo được, có cách đo, có mục tiêu. Các số mục tiêu đã được xác nhận ở mục 6.

| # | Tiêu chí | Cách đo | Mục tiêu |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Không còn credential dài hạn có quyền ghi prod trên laptop. | Số IAM user/access key có quyền ghi vào account prod; số quyền ghi prod gán thường trực cho người. | **0** |
| S2 | Không còn credential cloud dài hạn trong GitHub secrets. | Số AWS access key, GitHub PAT, Firebase/GCP key dài hạn được workflow dùng. | **0** |
| S3 | Mọi thay đổi prod, kể cả trong sự cố, có một người duyệt có tên, khác người làm, **trước** khi áp dụng. | Đối chiếu định kỳ (hằng tháng) các sự kiện ghi trong log cloud của prod với bản ghi phê duyệt. Đếm số thay đổi không khớp, và số thay đổi có thời điểm duyệt sau thời điểm áp dụng. | **0** / **0** |
| S4 | Engineer không mất tốc độ. | (a) Thời gian từ PR được tạo tới khi thay đổi hạ tầng chuẩn lên prod (median). (b) Thời gian chờ duyệt (median). (c) Vòng lặp ở non-prod không có bước duyệt mới. | (a) trong cùng ngày làm việc; (b) ≤ 1 giờ trong giờ làm việc; (c) đúng |
| S5 | Mọi cấu hình agent dùng trên máy engineer là cấu hình được duyệt. | % máy engineer nhận chính sách Claude Code của tổ chức; số engineer có thể tắt toàn bộ permission prompt mà không ai biết. | **100%** / **0** (phụ thuộc GĐ-6) |
| S6 | Mọi MCP server/plugin đang dùng nằm trong danh mục đã duyệt, và việc duyệt không thành nút cổ chai. | Số MCP/plugin đang dùng ngoài danh mục; thời gian xử lý yêu cầu thêm mới. | **0** ngoài danh mục; xử lý ≤ 5 ngày làm việc |
| S7 | Phát hiện và phản ứng có chủ, và sự cố không bị kẹt vì chờ duyệt. | Có lịch on-call có tên, gồm cả người duyệt; mọi alert prod về một kênh định tuyến; thời gian chờ duyệt cho thay đổi trong sự cố (24/7). | Lịch on-call có tên; 100% alert prod qua một kênh; chờ duyệt trong sự cố ≤ 15 phút, 24/7 (cần ít nhất primary + backup trực duyệt) |
| S8 | Evidence cho audit lấy ra nhanh. | Với một thay đổi prod chọn ngẫu nhiên: thời gian để trình ra đủ "ai đề xuất, ai duyệt, đã duyệt cái gì, cái gì được áp dụng, khi nào". | ≤ 30 phút, không cần hỏi người liên quan |
| S9 | Đọc dữ liệu thật trên prod chỉ xảy ra qua ngoại lệ được duyệt. | Số phiên agent/người đọc MED/NID/BANK trên prod không có yêu cầu được duyệt kèm theo; mọi yêu cầu có thời hạn và phạm vi tenant. | **0** phiên không có yêu cầu được duyệt |
| S10 | Code do agent viết đi qua cùng guardrail với code người viết, trước khi tới nhánh deploy. | % PR vào nhánh deploy có secret scan, kiểm tra dependency và SAST chạy và đạt; số lần push thẳng lên nhánh deploy; số secret bị phát hiện **sau** khi merge. | **100%** / **0** / **0** |
| S11 | Non-prod không chứa dữ liệu thật (GĐ-14). | Số lần copy dữ liệu prod xuống non-prod; kết quả quét định kỳ dữ liệu nhạy cảm trên non-prod. | **0** |

## 6. Câu hỏi kiểm tra lại (đã trả lời)

### Vòng 1

Người dùng trả lời trong chat, session 2 (2026-11-08).

| # | Câu hỏi | Đề xuất | Quyết định của người dùng |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Quy mô đội (GĐ-1) | 20–60 engineer, DevSecOps 1–2 người, không một reviewer duy nhất | Đồng ý |
| 2 | Reviewer khác tác giả? (GĐ-11) | Có (four-eyes); agent không là reviewer | Đồng ý, reviewer không phải người làm (tác giả hoặc agent tạo thay đổi). Hỏi lại: agent độc lập chỉ là bước review tự động bổ sung; phê duyệt chính thức phải là người |
| 3 | Agent đọc dữ liệu thật? (GĐ-9) | Không, cho tới khi có thoả thuận | Đồng ý mặc định là không; **cho phép theo từng trường hợp** khi có thoả thuận phù hợp, vì có lúc debug cần dữ liệu thật |
| 4 | Thay đổi khẩn cấp chưa duyệt? (GĐ-8) | Có, với 4 điều kiện và review sau | **Không đồng ý.** Mọi thay đổi prod phải được duyệt **trước**, kể cả trong sự cố |
| 5 | Ép cấu hình agent? (GĐ-6) | Laptop không tin cậy; kiểm soát chính ở cloud/CI | Đồng ý |
| 6 | Mục tiêu tốc độ (S4) | Duyệt ≤ 1 giờ trong giờ làm việc; ship trong ngày | Đồng ý |
| 7 | Phạm vi | Nguyên tắc chung cho tất cả; chi tiết cho AWS + GitHub Actions; GCP, k0s, Firebase ở mức áp dụng nguyên tắc | Đồng ý |
| 8 | Ưu tiên 30 ngày | (1) bỏ credential dài hạn trong CI, (2) thu hẹp quyền prod thường trực, (3) danh mục MCP/plugin | Đồng ý; on-call và monitoring ở giai đoạn 2 |

### Hệ quả cần mang sang bước thiết kế

- **Mâu thuẫn giữa câu 4 và câu 8.** Không có break-glass thì sự cố nào cũng cần một người duyệt có mặt ngay, 24/7.
  Nhưng on-call (P7) lại được xếp ở giai đoạn 2. Trong 30 ngày đầu, nếu thu hẹp quyền prod (ưu tiên 2) mà chưa có
  người duyệt trực, sự cố ngoài giờ có thể bị kẹt. Cần chọn một trong hai: (a) đưa "danh sách người duyệt trực"
  (chỉ phần tối thiểu của on-call) lên giai đoạn 1, hoặc (b) chỉ thu hẹp quyền prod sau khi có người duyệt trực.
  **Đã quyết (a):** đưa phần tối thiểu "danh sách người duyệt trực" (có tên, phủ 24/7) lên giai đoạn 1,

approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5); branch up to date, since there is no merge queue
(⚠️ R4.6 #1). `production` accepts only `main` (📖 R3.1.3).

- **Merge = deploy approval** only if the reusable deploy workflow alone references `production`,
  with no ref/SHA inputs, no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers, one
  concurrency group per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4; ⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c).
- **Two people per change:** one makes it, one approves it; the approver is always an engineer,
  never an agent (OD2, OD5). L3 changes need one approver too, who must own the path.
- **Incidents:** on-call engineers only approve; an incident responder writes the fix (OD7).

  primary, one backup (OD9). It does not co-own process-defining paths (`.github/**`, CODEOWNERS,
  agent config, catalogue) or the SCP stack, which only the L3 owner team approves (OD13); IAM-only
  stacks are deployable, so it co-owns them with the L3 owner team.

## Independent review: final pass A (rollout plan, compliance register, framework sync)

**Verdict: NOT READY.** There are no HIGH findings. Six MEDIUM findings remain, and Rule 4 requires fixing every HIGH and MEDIUM before the result goes to the user. All are small text fixes.

The checks that pass:
- **Links:** a script checked every relative link and GitHub-style anchor in `docs/**`, `README.md` and `diagrams/*.md`. Result: `bad 0`. Script: `/tmp/claude-1001/-home-do-hoang-minh-hung-papaya-devsecops-challenge/6db3dd9e-1a2b-4563-ab89-a7de7a1f8366/scratchpad/review-final-a/links.py`.
- **Moved content:** every phase-1, 2 and 3 item of the committed layer-8 table and "Phase-1 load" is in `03-rollout-plan.md`.
- **Removed evidence:** almost every audit-evidence item removed from the framework is in the register (one exception, M3).
- **Standards cross-reference:** the ISO, HIPAA and Vietnam IDs match research rows R5.1–R5.6 and R1.11.1.8. ISO stays ⚠️ throughout.
- **Rule 2 and Rule 3:** no secrets or personal data; all submitted text is in English.

**Framework size:** `wc -w docs/01-framework.md` = **10,974**. Committed HEAD was 11,381. The target was ~9.5–10k, so it is about 1k over. Reason: the sync edits from the examples findings added about 600 words, which cancelled most of the move.

More could move without losing the four-part layer structure. These are suggestions, not deletions:
- Owner-decision table: 910 words. It could go to an appendix file; OD-n stays as an ID.
- Layer 7 break-glass table: 458 words. It overlaps ADR-0005 and the engineer guide.
- Gaps table: 403 words.
- Layer 2 "Trade-off on AWS credentials": 366 words. It overlaps T10 and ADR-0007.
- Layer 3 "2 a.m." example: 168 words. The engineer guide §4 already covers it.

---

### MEDIUM

**M1. The rollout plan says it was moved "without changing its content" but adds content, including a new rule.**
- Where: `docs/03-rollout-plan.md:3`, `docs/01-framework.md:691-692` ("moved there unchanged").
- Content that is not in the committed layer 8:
  - Owner per item (`:24-43`). "Done when" (`:11`) is marked [design]; the owners are not.
  - Item **2.9** (`:83`, from OD15 and OD20; it has a source but is new to the plan).
  - Item 2.4 now adds "export of deploy run logs and risk-stop summaries" (`:78`).
  - The "Measured from" column in Metrics by phase (`:99-111`).
  - The "Engineering speed (S4)" risk (`:124-126`).
  - **A new rule:** "An exception never removes a hard prerequisite" (`:127-128`).
  - The phase-2 version floor is now 2.1.310 (`:46-48`); this one is a correct sync with layer 2.
- Effect: the status line is not accurate, and a rule appears that the owner never approved. The brief asked for "no new rules".
- Fix: change both status lines to "moved and expanded", list the additions, and mark them [design] for owner review. Or remove the new rule.

**M2. The S8 walk-through assumes one deploy run equals one commit equals one PR. It does not.**
- Where: `docs/04-compliance-mapping.md:96-97` (steps 2–3).
- Evidence: `examples/README.md` "Limits of the risk stop", concurrency bullet: GitHub cancels a pending run when a newer one arrives. "Some merged commits therefore have no deploy run of their own; the newer run deploys them too, and the change record must link both commits to that run."
- Effect: an auditor who starts from a CloudTrail write reaches the run's tip SHA. They may miss the earlier PR that actually caused the write, or report a false "unapproved change". This is the S8 honesty check.
- Fix: step 2 → "the commits on `main` between the previous successful deploy of this stack and the run's SHA". Step 3 → "each commit's squash-merged PR". Cite the examples concurrency limit.

**M3. An evidence statement was removed from layer 4 and appears nowhere in `docs/`.**
- Where: committed `docs/01-framework.md` layer 4: "MCP tool logging needs `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` (📖 R1.3.8); it stays off until we know whether it logs tool inputs (⚠️)." A grep of `docs/` and `README.md` returns no match. E8 sets it to `"0"`.
- Effect: Compliance no longer sees that there is no evidence of MCP use per tool. S6 evidence is plugin events only. The "nothing lost" check fails.
- Fix: add it to C-12 (Evidence: "MCP tool calls not logged: `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS` off, 📖 R1.3.8; ⚠️ whether it logs inputs") or to "Evidence gaps".

**M4. The threat model and the problem-control map were not updated for finding 19, OD21 and the ADR-0004 refinement.**
- `docs/05-threat-model.md:39` (T4) still says "`defaultMode` Manual with a read-only allowlist (D1, OD7b)".
- `docs/05-threat-model.md:69` says phase 1 has "no credential deny rules". Phase 1 now has `Read(~/.aws/**)` (OD21; framework `:204`, `:252-255`).
- `docs/06-problem-control-map.md:38` (P3b) still says "Read-only allowlist (D1, OD7b)".
- `docs/06-problem-control-map.md:55` (P9c) still says "risk stop shows the prod diff". ADR README `:36-38` and framework `:350-352` now say "which resources and properties change, not values".
- Effect: the threat model is marked "approved" but contradicts framework layer 2.
- Fix:
  - T4 and P3b: "built-in read-only commands plus two exact repo scripts (finding 19); `classifyAllShell` (OD21)".
  - Line 69: "no sandbox and only a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule".
  - P9c: "shows which prod resources and properties change".

**M5. The ADR README "Refinements since acceptance" leaves out ADR-0003.**
- Where: `docs/adr/README.md:33-45`; `docs/adr/0003-merge-to-main-is-the-approval-gate.md:30-32`.
- Evidence: the framework's "merge approval = deploy approval" conditions (`docs/01-framework.md:367-369`) now include squash-only merges (OD16) and "deploy only the current tip of `main`" (OD17). ADR-0003's list has neither, and the refinements section only covers ADR-0004 and ADR-0007.
- Effect: a reader of ADR-0003 gets an incomplete list of conditions. An old run re-run can roll prod back without approval, which is the reason for OD17.
- Fix: add an ADR-0003 bullet with OD16, OD17 and examples finding 4.

**M6. New 📖 markers in the framework have no research row and no link, and one cannot be traced.**
- Where:
  - `docs/01-framework.md:219` "network included (📖 sandboxing docs)".
  - `:208` "(📖 settings reference, examples E8)" for the 2.1.310 floor; same reason in `docs/03-rollout-plan.md:46-48`.
  - `:255` "(📖 permissions docs)".
  - `:369` "(📖 GitHub docs …)".
- Evidence:
  - The legend at `:15` defines 📖 only as an R*x.y* row. CLAUDE.md Rule 1 requires a link for 📖.
  - The 2.1.310 reason (monitors under `allowManagedHooksOnly`) appears only in a code comment at `examples/tests/test_claude_settings.py:238`. The E8 row of `examples/README.md` does not state it, so "see the E8 row" leads nowhere.
  - "Network included" is close to R1.6.2 (excluded commands run outside the sandbox) but is not quoted anywhere. The same sentence at `:224` keeps "⚠️ inference" for the same consequence.
- Fix:
  - Extend the legend with "📖 *doc name* → the link is in the cited examples finding".
  - Add the 2.1.310 reason and its link to the E8 row, or to research row 1.1.x.
  - For "network included", cite R1.6.2 or keep ⚠️.

---

### LOW

1. **Wrong marker row.** `docs/04-compliance-mapping.md:169`: "164.308(b), 164.314(a) (📖 R5.6)". R5.6 is an inference section; the framework legend `:16` lists 5.6 as ⚠️. The documented row is **R1.11.3.1**, which links eCFR 164.308(b) and 164.314(a). Fix: cite 📖 R1.11.3.1.
2. **Marker covers less than the sentence.** `docs/04-compliance-mapping.md:22`: "PRs, reviews, checks, git files and active rulesets: anyone with read access (📖 R3.2.2)". R3.2.2 covers only rulesets. Fix: limit the marker to rulesets, or mark the rest ⚠️.
3. **Actor field differs between two places.** `docs/04-compliance-mapping.md:119-121` (JIT walk-through) names the human only by session name. C-20 (`:73`) and layer 7 (`:622`) say "`onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name". Fix: align the two.
4. **"One row per control" is not quite complete.** `docs/04-compliance-mapping.md:8`. Not in the register:
   - session length and MFA (layer 1 `:163-164`);
   - CI-agent hardening (layer 5 `:506-512`);
   - the prod Pulumi flag limits (layer 3 `:372-373`).

   Fix: add rows, or say "main controls".
5. **Step 6 "in the window" is undefined.** `docs/04-compliance-mapping.md:100`. Fix: say "between the approval and `eventTime`".
6. **Stale "protection of the org trail" and a wrong E5 reference.** `docs/03-rollout-plan.md:76`: the wording is stale versus framework `:156-158` (finding 10: "deny changes to any trail in prod accounts"). "(E5)" also covers the outside-org write deny, which E5 does not contain (`examples/README.md` E5 row).
7. **"May not slip" still protects the old allowlist.** `docs/03-rollout-plan.md:68` and `:43` keep "the allowlist (D1 'immediately', OD7b)", which is now two npm scripts. The D1 and OD7b intent (fewer prompts) is now met by the built-in read-only set. In `docs/01-framework.md:213`, "D1's 'Manual + read-only allowlist'" reads as stale. In `:199`, "credential denies" are listed as phase 2 although phase 1 has the `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny; say "most credential denies".
8. **"Only prod write path" overstates.** `docs/03-rollout-plan.md:22` (heading) and framework `:693`: "the PR becomes the only prod write path". Minimal JIT (1.13) is also a write path. Fix: "the default prod write path".
9. **Item 1.4 cannot close in phase 1.** Its done-when, "No deploy from a laptop in CloudTrail for a month" (`docs/03-rollout-plan.md:29`), needs a month, but phase 1 is 30 days. Also dropped from item 1.13: "the revocation Deny SCP is deployed with the other SCPs in phase 2". Item 2.2 implies it.
10. **OD19 sentence is circular, and cites finding 14.** `docs/01-framework.md:159-160`: "only the Pulumi prod deploy role … (OD19; until OD20, 'only an approved prod Pulumi deploy')". The interim state is said twice and the target state (the IAM stack's own role, per the OD19 row `:765`) is never stated. Finding 14 is about the claim-data naming convention; finding 16 is the relevant one.
11. **Marker missing (finding 11).** `docs/01-framework.md:136-137`: "Some 'metadata' reads return configuration or secrets" has no marker. Finding 11 is ⚠️ (response contents from memory), except StackEvent, which is 📖. Fix: add "(mostly ⚠️, finding 11)".
12. **"Cover Papaya's whole stack" overstates (E8).** `docs/01-framework.md:207`. E8 marks several paths and env-var names ⚠️ and lists uncovered stores: Linear and Slack tokens, and files named by `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` or `KUBECONFIG`.
13. **G19 does not mention the hash check that OD18 needs.** `docs/01-framework.md:356` says "G19 closes it" (OD18), but the G19 row (`:735`) does not include "check that the stopped run's summary carries the same hash".
14. **Small losses in the evidence move.**
    - Layer 2 dropped "with PR approvals".
    - Layer 3 changed "linked by commit SHA and run ID" to "run ID".
    - Layer 5 dropped "the settings comparison in layer 7 covers the S2 exception meanwhile".
    - C-11 dropped the markers on the OTel fields (📖 research 6.6 D1; thresholds ⚠️).

    C-14 could reference C-21 for the environment-secret gap.
15. **Size and readability.** The register is 2,814 words (plan ~2,000) and the rollout plan 1,917 (plan ~1,500). That is acceptable, but an auditor would benefit from a "From phase" column in the register instead of "Ph n" inside the control text. Several framework lines are very long after the sync edits (e.g. `:137`, `:154`, `:187`, `:496`); this is cosmetic.

---

### Checked and correct
- All S1–S11 wordings match framing §5.
- OD, G, D, GĐ IDs and phase numbers in the register and rollout plan match the framework.
- The register's owners match layer 8, OD8, OD9, OD13 and OD14.
- "6 y" is correctly split: 📖 R5.2.9 for the rule, ⚠️ R5.7 #2 for applying it to change records.
- C-07's session name matches `examples/github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml:129`.
- The fail-safe CODEOWNERS line matches `examples/github/CODEOWNERS:22`.
- Layer 2 and layer 5 sync edits match findings 13, 19, 22, 23 and 25, and OD14–OD21. R6.9.3 does document the built-in read-only set.
- The S8 section is honest about phase 1: no change record or export, "realistic only from Ph 2 (⚠️)", Serverless `deploymentRole` attribution ⚠️, and no k0s or Firebase chain.
- Status changes on the threat model and the map are backed by `work/05-deliverable-plan.md` §0 and §5 Q7.
